correctness.rationale: For p>=11 the degree-(p+1) polynomial is squarefree exactly at a²≠4, hence has genus (p-1)/2. The standard Cartier coefficient rule gives an exact symmetric antidiagonal matrix with entries b_(2i-1). Reciprocal symmetry makes the twisted square diagonal with nonzero entries precisely where b_(2i-1) is nonzero, proving stable p-rank equals Cartier rank. The first and last antidiagonal entries equal ((p-1)/2)a, proving uniqueness of the rank-zero parameter and absence of rank one. Exact formal leading coefficients prove generic ordinarity. Source code independently checks coefficient expansion and ranks for prime fields p=11,...,43; no finite extrapolation is used.

originality.rationale: The assessed theorem is the all-prime p>=11 geometric family stratification and equality of stable p-rank with instantaneous Cartier rank, not the known Fermat seed or previously considered genus-three diagonal pencil. Borges-Gonçalves address binomial Fermat-type curves, and Kudo-Nakagawa-Takagi address a distinct genus-four C6 family. Full text/major portions were inspected, and targeted scientific and mathematical-record queries found no implication covering the variable-genus three-term family. Priority risk remains for old hyperelliptic/dihedral matrix formulae.
residual_risks: A historical dihedral hyperelliptic Hasse–Witt theorem might already encode this statement in equivalent language.

value.rationale: The family deforms a classical superspecial Fermat curve while genus grows with p. The uniform phenomenon that stable p-rank equals Cartier rank at every geometric parameter is a structural restriction on all positive-characteristic Jacobians in this pencil; the exact coefficient-stratum formula determines the invariants at every parameter, shows the superspecial point is isolated, excludes p-rank-one deformations for all p>=11, and gives a parity constraint in one congruence class. This is a natural full-family stratification beyond recomputing a single table or the known undeformed seed; no claim about Newton polygons or isomorphism census.
